title: Localization of Tor in the coefficient ring
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $M$ be an $R$-module, let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and let $A_{\mathfrak p}$ be the localization. For every $n\ge0$, the Tor groups are those of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], the canonical coefficient-localization map
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,A)_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,A_{\mathfrak p})$$
is an isomorphism. Consequently, vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,A)$ can be checked after localizing at every prime of $A$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00M8 (algebra-lemma-flat-base-change-tor), using its free-resolution argument for the flat localization A -> A_p.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and put $T=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)$. In the resolution computation of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], multiplication on the coefficient factor $A$ commutes with the differentials, so it makes $T$ an $A$-module. Set $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with its base ring and algebra both $A$, its first module $A$, and its second module $T$. Under $A\otimes_A T\cong T$, $a\otimes t\mapsto at$, it identifies $T_{\mathfrak p}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_A T$. Interchanging the tensor factors gives the isomorphism $\eta:T_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}T\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p}$, $t/s\mapsto t\otimes(1/s)$; its inverse sends $t\otimes(a/s)$ to $at/s$. These formulas also follow directly from the fraction relations in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and show that $\eta$ carries $t/1$ to $t\otimes1$.

The map $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ is localization at the multiplicative subset $S$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], hence is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Apply [lem-trf-tor-flat-base-change] to $R\to A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $M$. It gives an isomorphism $\beta:T\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A_{\mathfrak p})$. The composite $\beta\eta$ is the canonical map in the statement: using any projective resolution $F_\bullet$ of $M$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], a cycle $z\in F_n\otimes_R A$ represents $t\in T$, and both maps send $t/s$ to the homology class of $s^{-1}z$ in $F_\bullet\otimes_R A_{\mathfrak p}$. Here each pure tensor $f\otimes a$ in $z$ is sent to $f\otimes(a/s)$, so boundaries are sent to boundaries because the differential is coefficient-linear. Thus the displayed canonical map is an isomorphism for every $n\geq0$, including degree zero.

source.place: Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), Tag 00M8 (lemma-flat-base-change-tor, its free-resolution argument), and Tag 00LY (section-tor).

proof.text: If $T=0$, every fraction module $T_{\mathfrak p}$ is zero by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and Step 2 gives $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A_{\mathfrak p})=0$. Conversely, assume these latter Tor groups vanish for all primes of $A$. Step 2 gives $T_{\mathfrak p}=0$ for all such primes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to the zero map $T\to0$. Every maximal ideal is prime (the quotient is a field), and its localized map is $0\to0$, hence bijective. The cited statement makes $T\to0$ bijective, so $T=0$. This also covers the zero coefficient ring: the cited criterion imposes no nonzero-ring hypothesis.
